# ADR-003 — L1 audio readiness and isiXhosa voice path (D3 / C3)

Status: **Accepted** (Tope, 2026-10-21). Records decision D3 and closes CONFLICTS C3.

## Context

Elevation §16.2 calls for Stage-1 L1 content “with native audio for every item” in the first months. Curriculum §7 defines interim **human or gated, labelled TTS** per language, with native recordings replacing TTS by exposure rank while TTS remains for dynamic content. CONFLICTS C3 accepts the Curriculum definition for **L1 readiness** and preserves the Elevation bar as the **Native-verified** promotion criterion (ADR-001).

## Decision

### L1 readiness (C3)

A language may promote to **readiness level L1** when every learner-facing item in the promoted slice has **at least one playable audio attachment** that is either:

| Audio kind | Requirement |
|---|---|
| **Human-recorded** (`human_recorded`, `native_recorded`, or equivalent schema kind) | Valid `uri`; no synthetic tag |
| **Gated labelled TTS** (`tts_synthetic`) | Valid `uri`; **`synthetic_voice_tag`** present and visible to learners as **"Synthetic voice"** (ADR-001, CP-§0-24) |

Enforcement: `readiness.py` gate `L1` (`READINESS_L1_FAIL` when any item lacks gated audio). This is **not** the same as Native-verified audio quality.

### “Native audio for every item” (Elevation wording)

The Elevation phrase **does not** define L1. It defines the **Native-verified** bar:

- **G6 / G7** (Stage-1 A1 / A2 audio gates): human native recordings and speech-quality evals before high-stakes surfaces.
- **Promotion**: `label` → `native_verified` requires native-recorded audio on items and review gates (`readiness.py` promotion, `native_validation.py`, ADR-001 §6.6).
- **TTS replacement plan** (CP-§7): replace `tts_synthetic` on items by **exposure rank** as human recordings land; dynamic and uncached utterances may keep gated TTS longer.

### Tonal languages (Yoruba, Igbo, Hausa)

Vendor or custom **TTS must not ship** for `yo`, `ig`, or `ha` until the **tone-accuracy gate** passes (Curriculum H9; CONFLICTS C3):

- Eval sets and thresholds: `speech_eval.py` (`TONAL_TTS_LANGS`, `TTS_GATE_FAIL`, `tone_accuracy_gate_passed`).
- Tone scoring enablement requires calibrated judge agreement (`tone_scoring_calibration_report`).

Until the gate passes, L1 may use **human-recorded** audio only for those languages’ items (no ungated synthetic tone surfaces).

### isiXhosa voice path (D3)

| Track | Decision |
|---|---|
| **Commission** | **Custom isiXhosa voice now** (lead time; G8 dependency) — procurement and corpus contract owned by **EXT-12** |
| **Interim (Option A)** | **Matched corpus audio + text** for static curriculum items; **dynamic TTS disabled** until custom voice is enabled |
| **Coverage register** | `coverage_check.py` / `stage1_coverage.json`: `xh` `dynamic_tts` = `custom_voice_required`, `enabled: false`, `disabled_reason` cites **EXT-12** |

No learner-facing claim of “native Xhosa TTS” while dynamic TTS is disabled.

### Synthetic audio (ADR-001 AC5)

Every `tts_synthetic` clip uses the **"Synthetic voice"** learner tag without exception. Human clips never carry that tag.

## Verification (conformance checks for later cards)

| Check | Where enforced |
|---|---|
| L1 per-item gated audio | `readiness.py`, `test_readiness.py` |
| Synthetic voice tag | Common schema, ADR-001 tests |
| Tonal TTS gate | `speech_eval.py`, `test_speech_eval.py` |
| Xhosa dynamic TTS off + EXT-12 | `coverage_check.py`, `test_coverage_check.py` |
| Native-verified audio bar | `readiness.py` promotion, G6/G7 cards |
